newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle sales active at $64 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle sales active at $64 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold actively at a top of $64.00 per cwt before fading near midday when packers lowered bids to $63.00, feedlot sources said.
An estimated 40,000 to 45,000 head sold in Kansas and about 45,000 in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, sources there said.
Week-to-date trade in Kansas was estimated near 98,000 following Friday's active sales. Panhandle week-to-date movement was pegged near 100,000, they said.
Prices were steady with thin trade on Monday, but down $1.00 from Friday and down $2.00 from last week's top.
A two-week skid in fed cattle prices was attributed to an imminent expansion of market-ready cattle numbers and lighter-than-expected beef demand, feedlot sources said.

Cattle supplies were seen increasing each of the next six weeks as a result of active spring placements of cattle onto feed, they said. Packers also have plenty of contract cattle to draw from the next several weeks, some sources noted.
Beef demand reportedly was curbed by cool, wet weather that particularly cut into outdoor grilling and in turn, Memorial Day beef consumption, sources said.

The thin demand meant retailers may not need to replenish beef in retail coolers to the extent earlier expected for Father's Day promotions. Fathers Day is Sunday, June 15, and considered the last big weekend of the summer for beef consumption in the U.S.
